highlights.title: The Bentley Supersports: A stripped-out engineer's indulgence
highlights.summary: Bentley provided flights from Washington, DC, to Monterey, California, and accommodation so Ars could drive the Supersports, as well as ride in a preproduction Torcal EV, which we wrote about last week. Ars does not accept paid editorial content.
body: MONTEREY, Calif.—Last week, we brought news of the Bentley Torcal, a new electric vehicle that the luxury automaker has been cooking up at its HQ in Crewe, England. The company wants to attract new customers with its first battery EV, part of a plan to make sustainability as much a part of the brand's character as its high-end fit and finish. W12 engines have given way to V8 plug-in hybrid power, and the new Continental GT is all the better for it.

But around the same time as Ars got its first experience of that new PHEV two-door on a rather wet Spanish racetrack, some of Bentley's boffins were wondering what might happen if you also built one without the hybrid stuff.

Or all-wheel drive—something that has been a characteristic of every new road-going Bentley since the turn of the century. That would certainly cut the curb weight. So, too, would leaving out the rear seats. That sort of idea leads down a well-trodden path for some OEMs, and Porsche in particular is famous for making stripped-out road cars inspired by its race cars and making money from them, too.

highlights.title: MIT Quantum Initiative launches postdoctoral fellowship program
highlights.summary: The Institute welcomes its first cohort of QMIT Fellows this fall to advance interdisciplinary quantum research.
body: The MIT Quantum Initiative (QMIT) has launched a new postdoctoral fellowship program to accelerate interdisciplinary quantum research and develop the next generation of scientific leaders working at the frontiers of quantum science and technology.

Supported by a grant from the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation, the program reflects QMIT’s vision of expanding the boundaries of quantum science by encouraging researchers to connect quantum approaches with other disciplines and emerging applications.

As opportunities in quantum research expand, investing in outstanding early-career researchers has never been more important. These fellowships are designed to help cultivate the next generation of quantum leaders, providing the resources and collaborative environment needed to advance transformative research at MIT.

highlights.title: Saka earns hard-fought win for Arsenal at Villa
highlights.summary: Bukayo Saka's goal just before the hour mark was enough for champions Arsenal to maintain their perfect start with a 1-0 win over Aston Villa at Villa Park.
body: This fixture was one of the few matches that the Gunners lost in winning the Premier League title last season but Saka's close-range effort decided what was a tight game despite an improved showing from Unai Emery's much-changed Aston Villa line-up.

Villa were four down after 31 minutes in that astonishing capitulation at Brighton on the opening weekend but they showed far more resilience against the Gunners from the outset. Emiliano Buendia crashed the ball against David Raya's crossbar on 12 minutes.

Mikel Arteta's men, unchanged from the win over Coventry, were their usual probing selves, asking searching questions from set pieces and controlling possession for long periods. But Gabriel's mistimed header was as close as they came in the first half.

Christos Tzolis was substituted at half-time having been booked and running the risk of a red card after that, but the introduction of Eberechi Eze worked out well. Arsenal ramped up the pressure in the second half with the ever-impressive Saka to the fore.

highlights.title: ‘Obsession’ Producer Files Lawsuit Claiming She Was Cut Out of Profits Despite “Rescuing” Cut
highlights.summary: Producers James Harris and Mark Lane are accused by fellow producer Leonora Ann Darby of making compensation promises that they did not keep when the Curry Barker feature became a massive hit.
body: An executive producer on Obsession who allegedly “rescued“ the box office smash hit from a bad edit is suing two fellow producers for cutting her out of her share of the profits.

In a lawsuit filed in California state court on Monday, producer Leonora Ann Darby accuses Tea Shop Productions‘ co-founders and her colleagues James Harris and Mark Lane of reneging on an agreement to treat her as an equal producer at the company and not acknowledging her key role on Obsession, with financial ramifications.

Though she was formally credited as an executive producer on Obsession, the lawsuit argues Darby acted as a lead producer within the functional, internal definition used by Tea Shop Productions. Conveniently, the lawsuit alleges, once Obsession became a major hit — recently crossing $500 million worldwide on a reported $750,000 budget — she was boxed out of net profit participation previously promised for projects she lead-produced, despite her significant work on the film.

highlights.title: Apple shares ‘shocking evidence’ against former employee accused of stealing company data for OpenAI
highlights.summary: Apple says it has evidence that a former employee destroyed evidence of data theft after learning he was under investigation.
body: In its lawsuit against OpenAI, Apple filed what it calls “shocking evidence” to bolster its allegations that former employees stole trade secrets for OpenAI’s benefit. These new details emerged after the legal counsel for former Apple employee Chang Liu — who now works at OpenAI — handed over Liu’s old Apple work laptop for investigation earlier this month.

Apple now alleges that Liu used a confidential Apple circuit schematic in his work at OpenAI, as well as a tool that shares a name with an internal Apple engineering application. The company claims that OpenAI was “well-aware” of Liu’s access to Apple data, and that Liu enlisted OpenAI colleague Yu-Ting Peng to help destroy evidence in June when he learned that Apple was investigating him.

“The MacBook represents the very limited information Defendants provided so far (and only after weeks of delay), and shows Apple is not conducting ‘fishing expeditions’ but that its trade secrets are being used and evidence is being destroyed,” the filing reads.
points: Apple says it has evidence that a former employee destroyed evidence of data theft after learning he was under investigation.

highlights.title: The Bizarre Cult Sci-fi Classic ‘Donnie Darko’ Is Now Free to Watch
highlights.summary: A cult classic isn't necessarily a movie everyone loved when it came out. Sometimes it's the movie that found its audience years later — passed around between friends, endlessly quoted, rediscovered on late-night cable, and eventually embraced by a devoted group of fans.
body: Some are straightforward genre favorites, like The Evil Dead or The Warriors. Others are considerably stranger. Heathers, Napoleon Dynamite, and The Rocky Horror Picture Show all have wildly different sensibilities, but they share that same ability to inspire the kind of devotion that turns a movie into something bigger than its original release.

Richard Kelly's Donnie Darko is now available to watch for free on YouTube, giving anyone who somehow missed the 2001 cult classic a chance to see one of the strangest and most enduring movies of its era without paying for a rental or subscription.

Donnie Darko follows Donnie Darko (Jake Gyllenhaal), a troubled teenager living with his family in suburban Virginia. One night, Donnie is visited by a mysterious figure named Frank wearing a creepy rabbit costume. Frank tells him that the world will end in 28 days, setting Donnie on a bizarre path involving time travel, alternate realities and an increasingly complicated series of events that may or may not be connected.
The movie features an unusually stacked cast for an offbeat sci-fi drama, including Jena Malone, Maggie Gyllenhaal, Drew Barrymore, Patrick Swayze, Seth Rogen, and Mary McDonnell.
points: A cult classic isn't necessarily a movie everyone loved when it came out.

highlights.title: The Hugging Face hack could indicate cultural issues at OpenAI
highlights.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. By now you’ve probably heard about last month’s major AI security incident, in which OpenAI agents escaped their sandbox and hacked into the AI platform Hugging…
body: The day before OpenAI released that report, I spoke with David Krueger, a computer science professor and prominent alignment expert who took leave from the University of Montreal to found and lead an AI safety nonprofit called Evitable. He said what he had really hoped to see in the report was an analysis of the human factors behind the incident.

“When you look at accidents and incidents, oftentimes people try to find the technical source of failure, but that can give a very inaccurate and misleading sense of why the failure occurred,” he said. “If people are just cutting corners all the time, if people are not in a culture that prioritizes safety and has appropriate incentives and structures, [accidents] are kind of bound to happen.”

The report did not meet Krueger’s hopes. Its 38 pages detail a multi-month progression of agent misbehavior that culminated in the Hugging Face hack, explore the technical reasons why that misbehavior occurred, and enumerate the steps being taken to prevent similar events in the future. But there’s no consideration of the role that company culture may have played in the incident, and the report includes few references to specific human errors.

body: The Northern Irishman finished in a seven-way tie for fourth at the FedEx Cup over the weekend, finishing five shots off tournament winner Scottie Scheffler despite showing earlier signs of promise.
Now 37, six-time major winner McIlroy admitted his "fuse was shorter than it used to be" before the final round at the East Lake Golf Club.
He had arrived in Atlanta off the back of three weeks of competing in a row, something he admitted he would never exceed again despite still managing a fourth-place finish over the weekend.
"That just tells you how good he is," Lee told the Sky Sports Golf Podcast. "But I think Rory's body language this week wasn't great. He looked slightly… is grumpy the right word?

highlights.summary: September will see an absolute deluge of new video game releases across all platforms, and Xbox is no exception. It's been a turbulent summer for Microsoft's gaming platform, with another hefty hike to hardware prices beginning Aug.
body: For those searching for a bit of distraction to offset all that grim news, there's a heaping helping of new games to play. Many of these come from third-party developers like Capcom, CD Projekt Red, and Remedy Entertainment, though the Microsoft-owned Mojang is in the mix with a new Minecraft spin-off at the end of the month. We'll have to wait a little bit longer for big-ticket Xbox exclusives like Gears of War: E-Day (Oct. 6) and the new Fable (Feb. 23, 2027). That said, Xbox players have plenty of exciting new games to sink their teeth into this September, including several titles that are already generating Game of the Year buzz. Here are a few of our top picks.

Fancy a little romance? This open-world, dark fantasy RPG developed by a team of ex- Witcher 3 devs features multiple potential love interests and dedicated questlines. You'll play as Coen, a broody, man-bunned fellow in 14th-century central Europe. He's a human by day, vampire by night. During the course of the story, you'll be forced to choose whether to preserve your humanity or preserve your cursed powers. It's great to have options, but embracing the path of a himbo bloodsucker seems like the most fun.

highlights.title: Amazon rigged billions in ad pricing, lawsuit from states and US watchdog alleges
highlights.summary: Amazon responded to the lawsuit, arguing the US Federal Trade Commission "misunderstands" their ad market.
body: The US Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and a bipartisan group of 22 states has filed a lawsuit alleging Amazon secretly overcharged more than a million advertising customers by manipulating online auctions it uses to set ad prices.
The FTC and states say in their lawsuit filed Monday that the alleged scheme has likely netted the company $20bn from advertising customers since 2019.
"Amazon overrides and replaces the actual auction results with higher prices set by Amazon to increase its profits," says a complaint filed in the company's home state of Washington.
In a statement to the BBC, Amazon "strongly disagrees" with the premise that it misled advertisers and called the suit "misguided."
points: Amazon responded to the lawsuit, arguing the US Federal Trade Commission "misunderstands" their ad market.

highlights.title: 'GTA 6' Hype is Sending PS5 Pro Prices Through the Roof
highlights.summary: After 13 years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto 6 finally gave fans something substantial to obsess over this weekend. Rockstar's 26-minute extended look showed off Jason and Lucia's latest adventures in Vice City, along with some seriously impressive visuals, from destructible environments and…
body: The footage was captured on PS5 hardware, and the hype has already spilled over into the console market. Nobody may be more excited about GTA 6 than the third-party sellers cashing in on PS5 Pro demand.

Following the GTA 6 extended look, the PS5 Pro has become considerably harder to find at its normal price in the U.S. Major retailers have been running out of stock, leaving third-party sellers to take advantage of the sudden demand.

At Walmart and Best Buy, via TechPowerUp, third-party listings for the PS5 Pro have climbed to as high as $1,400, including a $1,299.99 listing sold and shipped by a third-party seller. That's a significant jump from the console's $899 price. highlights.summary: A jury has found Duane “Keffe D” Davis guilty of orchestrating the 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur. After a day of closing arguments, Davis was found guilty of murder with the use of a deadly weapon with the intent to promote, further or assist a criminal gang, according to ABC News. Davis, 63, faces a
body: During his closing arguments, prosecutor Binu Palal said that the case was “drenched in circumstantial evidence” and corroborating witnesses, in addition to Davis’ own statements over the years to media and in his own memoir to show that he was guilty of aiding the murder. “For nearly 18 years, Duane Davis has told the police, television, books, YouTube interviewers — anybody that will listen, he has told — he is responsible for the murder of Tupac Shakur,” said Palal. “Tell him you hear him — find him guilty.”
Davis’ attorney Michael Sanft, meanwhile, argued that the only proof that Davis was responsible for Shakur’s murder was through his own confessions, which did not constitute real evidence.
“We have to ask ourselves the question really at this particular point: Why are we here 30 years later if Duane Davis had actually confessed — truly confessed?” he said.
Davis is scheduled to be sentenced on October 13 and will be held without bail. He shared that he plans to appeal the sentence once it’s handed down.

highlights.title: Shein Makes IPO Debut at $26.5B Valuation, a Fraction of Previous Estimates
highlights.summary: Ultra-fast fashion giant Shein went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange this morning at a fraction of its former value. How did its IPO efforts go awry?
body: Ultra-fast fashion giant Shein is now public, following several years of false starts. The Singapore-based company priced shares at HK$48.56 ($6.20), raising $1.74 billion and valuing it at $26.5 billion in pre-market trading. Shares fell 7% when the market opened on Tuesday morning.

It’s been a rocky road to an IPO for Shein, whose valuation has steadily declined for several years amid geopolitical headwinds. It peaked in 2022 at $98.2 billion, sinking to $66 billion at the time of its most recent funding round in May 2023. And most recently, ahead of the IPO, the company was targeting a valuation of $27 billion, after pricing 280 billion shares between HK$47.60 ($6.07) and HK$49.50 ($6.31), with the goal of raising $1.77 billion.
Shein’s fast fashion machine was once thought to be an investor’s gold mine. What happened?

highlights.title: Trump admin shelves Cyclospora research despite record-breaking outbreak
highlights.summary: The Trump administration is halting vital federal research on the foodborne parasite Cyclospora, despite the record-breaking, nationwide outbreak of the diarrheal pathogen, according to Politico.
body: Of the three research programs that represent nearly all of the Cyclospora work at the US Department of Agriculture, two have been defunded, and the third is about to lose every scientist working on it. The Trump administration is shuttering the USDA’s Beltsville Agricultural Research Center near Washington, DC, and moving its work to a location in Iowa. That includes relocating the remaining Cyclospora research.

Although the research is still funded, insiders told Politico that not one of the scientists working on the project plans to relocate from Maryland to Iowa. Instead, they are either retiring, being reassigned to a different project, or leaving the USDA’s research services.
“They will have no parasitologists,” one USDA employee told Politico. “There will be a big knowledge gap.”

The US is experiencing the largest Cyclospora outbreak ever recorded. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has tallied nearly 30,000 confirmed and probable cases this summer. At least 922 people have been hospitalized with cyclosporiasis, and two have died. Since 2018, the US has generally reported between 2,000 and 5,000 cases, though the US reported 1,180 cases in 2025.

highlights.title: The Pentagon now has its own version of ChatGPT and Grok
highlights.summary: Versions of OpenAI's ChatGPT and SpaceXAI's Grok will join Google's Gemini on the Pentagon's central portal for AI tools.
body: The Pentagon has launched versions of OpenAI’s ChatGPT and xAI’s Grok, giving 3 million civilian and military personnel access to generative AI tools that have been tailored to “warfighter needs.”
ChatGPT Mil and Grok for Government — custom versions of the popular consumer generative AI tools — are now part of GenAI.mil, a centralized, secure portal launched last year.

GenAI.mil, which offered Google Gemini when it first launched, is designed to give Department of Defense employees access to commercial frontier AI models without sending sensitive government data through ordinary consumer channels. In particular, the official military version is exempt from the data collection that is difficult to avoid in consumer tech products.

And according to the Department of Defense, the generative AI portal has proven popular. GenAI.mil has already onboarded more than 1.7 million unique users out of the department’s 3 million personnel, according to the department.

body: When not intended, smudged eye makeup can ruin a look; but unfortunately—whether due to the heat or constantly getting in and out of the water at the beach or pool—it’s often unavoidable. The solution, then, is to use products specifically formulated to withstand the day’s challenges. You likely already have a waterproof mascara on hand, but let us make the case for an e yeshadow stick that’s heat-, sweat-, and impromptu-dive proof. Behold: let us introduce you to the Kiko Milano Eyeshadow Stick.

While some eyeshadow pigments go on grainy, and deliver little to no pigment in the process, this one offers a creamy texture that makes it easy to apply and comfortable to wear. The color itself lasts all day—depositing flawless color wherever it’s placed.

Though you might imagine you need to swipe the little domed pencil with precision, there’s less of an art to it than you’d imagine. As professional makeup artist Colby Smith previously told Vogue, think of an eyeshadow stick as a jumbo eyeliner. Offering versatility and simplicity simultaneously, all you need to do is swipe on the color where you want it.

body: Since its launch in 1998, Ars Technica has been known for its depth of community. If all you’re doing is checking out the front page and the discussion threads that sit beneath each story, you’re missing out on more than you realize.

The Ars OpenForum is a place for readers to ask questions, compare notes, argue (without being jerks to each other), and go down all sorts of rabbit holes. Our Hardware and Tweaking forums cover PC builds, networking, mobile computing, CPUs and motherboards, A/V, and just about any other hardware-related topic you can think of. Stop by the Operating Systems & Software forums for in-depth discussion on Windows, macOS, or Linux or just to have a good, friendly argument over why your preferred OS rules.

We’ve also spent some significant time and effort cleaning up ancient markdown and HTML tags that made some of our all-time classic forum threads almost unreadable. Now you can read the story of Fugly the Octopus, the time someone accidentally swallowed the 7 key on his keyboard, or just another customer service rant —in all of their original glory.

highlights.title: New York Governor Kathy Hochul thinks AI should be ‘less evil’
highlights.summary: Today, I’m talking with New York Governor Kathy Hochul, and I’ll just warn you — this episode moves really fast. It’s an election year, after all, with a shocking amount of tech policy at stake, and Governor Hochul has taken strong positions on almost every major tech issue there is.
body: For example, Meta just reached a settlement with dozens of states, including New York, which will restrict how teens use platforms like Instagram in very specific ways. Governor Hochul is a strong supporter of those restrictions and more, as you’ll hear. But those come with a cost — widespread age verification means adults will also have to show ID to use the internet, which will essentially make it impossible to be anonymous online.

So I asked about that, and if these new restrictions amount to Meta conceding in a lawsuit that these kinds of regulations on speech might not pass First Amendment scrutiny if the governor were to try and impose them in a law.

I had similar questions about New York’s restrictions on ghost guns, which prevent 3D printers from printing gun parts. That law is already being challenged — not in courts, but by activists like Cody Wilson, who runs the largest database of 3D-printable gun files and who has started altering those files in a process he calls “Hochulization” in order to show the ban is technically toothless. I asked the governor about this, and, well, you’ll hear her challenge Cody right back.
